system.description:
Widely reviled, graverobbers are a specific form of thief which trade in the trinkets and mementos of the dead in the best of times and in the value of their fresh corpse in the worst of times.

Those who know of your history will likely despise you. Call you a desecrator or worse. But sometimes one has to do what they have to do to survive, in the end, lest they join those already in the grave. So long as there are necromancers and fleshwrights, there will be a desire for fresh bodies.

Ability Score Increase: Constitution +1, any other attribute +1

Skill Proficiencies: Deception, Stealth

Tool Proficiencies: None

Suggested Equipment (Cost 8 gold): Hemp rope 50ft, hooded lantern, shovel

Feature: Gravedigger. A job no one wishes to do, and few are willing to do: you’ve long become skilled at digging perfectly useable holes in the ground. With 3 hours of labor you can dig a grave instead of the usual 8. In communities with a cemetary, this affords you a moderate lifestyle for a day’s work, or a poor one in communities without as you are relegated to manual labor. In communities with necromancers or scientists looking for fresh cadavers, however, 3 hours of work secures a moderate lifestyle for a week. In addition, you can clear rubble in half the normal time.

Adventures and Advancement: While there’s precious room for advancement in the digging of holes industry, if you’re willing to work for people who aren’t on the up and up, you can get yourself a rich lifestyle digging up bodies for a necromancer if you work 3 hours each day. The downside, of course, is that law enforcement and graveyard guardians become more and more severe as a resurrectionist plies their grisly trade.

Connections and Memento: Roll 1d10, choose, or make up your own.
